title: Finland Presidential Election
description: Alexander Stubb (National Coalition) defeats Pekka Haavisto in the runoff with 51.6% of the vote, succeeding Sauli Niinistö, who was term-limited.

title: Portugal Legislative Election
description: Snap election after PM António Costa's resignation. Centre-right Democratic Alliance (AD) wins most seats (80 of 230) without a majority; Chega becomes third-largest party with 50 seats.

title: Slovakia Presidential Election
description: Peter Pellegrini defeats Ivan Korčok in the runoff with 53.1%, succeeding Zuzana Čaputová, who did not seek re-election.

title: Croatia Parliamentary Election
description: HDZ wins most seats (61 of 151) but loses its majority. Andrej Plenković secures a third term as PM in coalition with the right-wing Homeland Movement (DP).

title: Lithuania Presidential Election
description: Incumbent Gitanas Nausėda re-elected president, defeating PM Ingrida Šimonytė in the runoff with 75.3% of the vote.

title: Belgium Federal Election
description: Flemish nationalist N-VA becomes largest party with 24 of 150 seats. Bart De Wever is sworn in as PM of the 'Arizona' coalition on 3 February 2025, about 240 days later.

title: European Parliament Elections
description: EU citizens vote across 27 member states for 720 MEPs. Centre-right EPP remains largest group with 188 seats, far-right makes significant gains.

title: UK General Election
description: Labour Party wins massive landslide, ending 14 years of Conservative rule. Keir Starmer becomes Prime Minister.

title: France Legislative Election
description: Snap election called by Macron after EU elections setback. Left-wing New Popular Front wins most seats (about 180 of 577) but no majority, producing a hung parliament; Michel Barnier becomes PM in September.

title: Austria National Election
description: Freedom Party (FPÖ) wins most seats with 28.8%, the first far-right first place in post-war Austria. It is left out of government: an ÖVP–SPÖ–NEOS coalition under Christian Stocker takes office in March 2025.

title: Lithuania Parliamentary Election
description: Social Democrats (LSDP) win most seats (52 of 141) after the 27 October runoff round, replacing Ingrida Šimonytė's centre-right government; Gintautas Paluckas becomes PM.

title: Bulgaria Parliamentary Election
description: GERB–SDS remains largest party in the sixth snap election since 2021. Rosen Zhelyazkov forms a GERB-led minority government in January 2025.

title: Romania Presidential Election (Round 1, Annulled)
description: Pro-Russian candidate Călin Georgescu surprises with first-place finish. Constitutional Court annuls the election on 6 December over alleged Russian interference.

title: Romania Parliamentary Election
description: PSD remains largest party while far-right AUR finishes second with 18%. A pro-European PSD–PNL–UDMR coalition under Marcel Ciolacu takes office on 23 December.

title: Croatia Presidential Election
description: President Zoran Milanović wins re-election in a landslide runoff, taking 74.7% against HDZ-backed Dragan Primorac.

title: Germany Federal Election
description: CDU/CSU wins with 28.5% under Friedrich Merz; AfD second with 20.8%. Merz is elected chancellor on 6 May 2025 at the head of a CDU/CSU–SPD coalition.

title: Romania Presidential Election (Round 1, Re-run)
description: Far-right George Simion (AUR) leads first round of re-run election with 41%, following annulment of the 2024 vote due to foreign interference.

title: Portugal Parliamentary Election
description: Third election in just over three years. Democratic Alliance (AD) wins 91 of 230 seats, short of a majority; Chega overtakes the Socialists for second place. Luís Montenegro stays on as PM.

title: Poland Presidential Election (Round 1)
description: Centrist Rafał Trzaskowski (31.4%) and PiS-backed Karol Nawrocki (29.5%) advance to runoff in closely contested first round.

title: Romania Presidential Election (Runoff)
description: Pro-EU Nicușor Dan defeats far-right George Simion with 53.6% in a comeback from second place in round one. Election seen as crucial test for Romania's Western alignment.

title: Poland Presidential Election (Runoff)
description: Karol Nawrocki wins with 50.9% against Warsaw mayor Rafał Trzaskowski in narrow runoff.

title: Czech Republic Parliamentary Election
description: Andrej Babiš's ANO wins with 34.5% and 80 of 200 seats, ousting Petr Fiala's centre-right coalition. Babiš becomes PM in December 2025 in coalition with SPD and Motorists.

title: Ireland Presidential Election
description: Left-wing independent Catherine Connolly wins with 63.4% of first-preference votes, defeating Fine Gael's Heather Humphreys.

title: Portugal Presidential Election (Round 1)
description: Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa is term-limited. Socialist António José Seguro (about 31%) and Chega leader André Ventura (about 23.5%) advance to runoff.

title: Portugal Presidential Election (Runoff)
description: António José Seguro defeats André Ventura in the runoff with 66.8% of the vote.

title: Slovenia Parliamentary Election
description: Robert Golob's Freedom Movement narrowly finishes first with 29 of 90 seats, one ahead of SDS, but loses its majority. Janez Janša forms a right-wing coalition and becomes PM for a fourth time.

title: Denmark General Election
description: Snap election: Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats remain largest party (38 seats) on their lowest vote share since 1903. Neither bloc wins a majority; Frederiksen forms a centre-left minority government in June.

title: Hungary Parliamentary Election
description: Péter Magyar's Tisza Party wins a two-thirds supermajority (141 of 199 seats), ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year Fidesz government. Magyar becomes PM on 9 May 2026.

title: Bulgaria Parliamentary Election
description: Snap election after the Zhelyazkov government resigns amid anti-corruption protests. Former president Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria wins an absolute majority (131 of 240 seats) in the eighth parliamentary election since 2021.

title: Malta General Election
description: Robert Abela's Labour Party wins a fourth consecutive election with 51.8% of the vote, defeating Alex Borg's Nationalist Party.

title: Estonia Presidential Election
description: Alar Karis does not seek a second term. Riigikogu elects Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise president in the first round with 71 of 101 votes.

title: Sweden General Election
description: Social Democrats become largest party with 28%. The centre-left opposition wins 176 of 349 seats against 173 for the Tidö parties; Ulf Kristersson resigns and Magdalena Andersson begins government talks.

title: Latvia Parliamentary Election
description: Andris Kulbergs's United List becomes largest party with 35.8% and 41 of 100 Saeima seats.

title: Czech Republic Senate Election
description: Scheduled first round (9–10 October) for 27 of the Senate's 81 seats, with runoffs on 16–17 October.

title: Bulgaria Presidential Election
description: Scheduled first round of presidential election; a runoff follows if no candidate wins a majority. Incumbent Iliana Iotova seeks a full term.

title: Spain General Election
description: Scheduled snap election to the Congress of Deputies and Senate, called by PM Pedro Sánchez after parliament rejected his housing decrees.

title: Estonia Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled Riigikogu election for all 101 seats, due by 7 March 2027.

title: France Presidential Election (Round 1)
description: Scheduled first round. Incumbent Emmanuel Macron is term-limited and cannot stand.

title: France Presidential Election (Runoff)
description: Scheduled second round, held if no candidate wins an absolute majority in the first round.

title: Greece Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled parliamentary election, due by 25 July 2027. PM Kyriakos Mitsotakis has signalled a spring 2027 vote.

title: Italy Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled election to the Chamber of Deputies and Senate, due by 22 December 2027.

title: Cyprus Presidential Election
description: Scheduled presidential election, due in February 2028. Incumbent Nikos Christodoulides is eligible for a second term.

title: Luxembourg General Election
description: Scheduled Chamber of Deputies election, due on or before 8 October 2028.

title: Lithuania Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled Seimas election, with a second round two weeks later.

title: Romania Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled election to the Chamber of Deputies and Senate, due on or before 30 November 2028.

title: Austria Presidential Election
description: Scheduled presidential election, due by 2028. Incumbent Alexander Van der Bellen is term-limited and cannot stand.

title: Germany Federal Election
description: Scheduled Bundestag election, due on or before 25 March 2029.

title: Slovakia Presidential Election
description: Scheduled presidential election, due by April 2029 (at least 60 days before the term ends in June). President Peter Pellegrini is eligible for re-election.

title: Lithuania Presidential Election
description: Scheduled presidential election. Incumbent Gitanas Nausėda is term-limited.

title: European Parliament Elections
description: Scheduled for 7–10 June 2029: EU citizens across 27 member states elect 720 Members of European Parliament for the 2029–2034 term.

title: Belgium Federal Election
description: Scheduled Chamber of Representatives election, due in 2029 and held together with the European Parliament elections.

title: France Legislative Election
description: Scheduled National Assembly election, due by June 2029 unless the Assembly is dissolved earlier.

title: Portugal Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled Assembly of the Republic election, due by 14 October 2029.

title: Austria National Election
description: Scheduled National Council election, due by October 2029.

title: Czech Republic Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled Chamber of Deputies election, due by October 2029.

title: Croatia Presidential Election
description: Scheduled presidential election, due by January 2030. Incumbent Zoran Milanović is term-limited.

title: Finland Presidential Election
description: Scheduled first round of presidential election. Incumbent Alexander Stubb is eligible for re-election.

title: Ireland General Election
description: Scheduled Dáil Éireann election, due no later than January 2030.

title: Slovenia Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled National Assembly election, due on or before 22 March 2030.

title: Denmark General Election
description: Scheduled Folketing election, due on or before 23 March 2030.

title: Poland Presidential Election (Round 1)
description: Scheduled first round, due by May 2030. Incumbent Karol Nawrocki is eligible for re-election.

title: Hungary Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled National Assembly election, due in April or May 2030.

title: Poland Presidential Election (Runoff)
description: Scheduled second round, held if no candidate wins a majority in the first round.

title: Sweden General Election
description: Scheduled Riksdag election, held on the second Sunday of September.

title: Latvia Parliamentary Election
description: Scheduled Saeima election, held on the first Saturday of October.

title: Portugal Presidential Election (Round 1)
description: Scheduled presidential election, due in January 2031. Incumbent António José Seguro is eligible for a second term.

title: Ireland Presidential Election
description: Scheduled presidential election, due by November 2032 at the end of Catherine Connolly's seven-year term.

title: Cyprus Presidential Election
description: Scheduled presidential election, due by February 2033.

title: European Parliament Elections
description: Scheduled election, due by June 2034: EU citizens elect Members of European Parliament for the 2034–2039 term.
